parameters.content:
## Weekly specials video from your menu sheet

Every Monday at 9am this workflow reads your Google Sheet menu, takes the rows
marked `ThisWeek = TRUE`, and renders a 1080x1920 specials reel with Zvid —
a sizzle hook, one photo card per dish with a price chip, and a booking CTA,
all in your brand colours. Ready for Instagram Reels and Facebook.

### Setup (about five minutes)

1. **Zvid API key** — create one at https://app.zvid.io/api-keys
   Add an n8n **Header Auth** credential: name `x-api-key`, value = your key.
   Attach it to *Validate project (free)*, *Save draft to editor*,
   *Submit render* and *Get render status*.
2. **Google Sheets** — attach your Google Sheets credential to *Read menu sheet*
   and pick your spreadsheet + sheet there. Column layout is in the note beside it.
3. **Open `Config`** — restaurant name, tagline, handle, address, brand colours,
   fonts, timings. Every knob lives in this one node.
4. Run **Test manually**. This workflow renders for real out of the box, so the
   **first run spends credits** — about **16** for the 4-dish default. When it
   finishes, click **▶ Watch video** to play the reel inside n8n.
5. Prefer a free preview first? Set `dryRun: true` in `Config` *before* that
   run: it validates, quotes the exact credit cost and saves a draft with an
   **editorLink** — nothing is charged. Set it back to `false` to render.
6. **Activate** the workflow to pick up the Monday 9am schedule.

### Cost per video

The 4-dish default quotes **16 Zvid credits** (~15s); expect roughly **13-18**
for 3-5 dishes. *Validate project (free)* runs before every render and returns
the exact quote for your own menu — with the shipped `dryRun: false` the
render then proceeds automatically. Free accounts include credits to test.

## The menu sheet

*Read menu sheet* expects these columns (row 1 = headers; order, casing and
spacing do not matter — `Photo URL` works too):

| Column | Example |
| --- | --- |
| Dish | Wild Mushroom Pappardelle |
| Description | Hand-cut pasta, porcini cream, shaved pecorino. |
| Price | $19 |
| PhotoUrl | https://…/pasta.jpg |
| ThisWeek | TRUE |

- **ThisWeek** — `TRUE`, `yes`, `1` or `x` all count. The video features the
  first **5** marked rows (3-5 reads best); extras are skipped and reported.
- **Price** — free text, bring your own currency symbol. Leave it empty to
  hide the price chip for that dish.
- **Description** — one or two short lines; anything past ~220 characters is
  trimmed with an ellipsis so the card never overflows.
- **PhotoUrl** — a direct https image link; portrait shots crop best on the
  1080x1920 card. If empty, a polished food photo from `fallbackDishPhotos`
  in Config steps in so the video never breaks.

## Free dry run — opt in from Config

`Config` ships with `dryRun: false`, so a normal run goes straight past this
branch and renders for real.

Set `dryRun: true` in **Config** and the workflow stops here instead: it saves
the project as a **draft** and reports an **editorLink** like
`https://editor.zvid.io/?project=prj_...`

Open it to watch the reel, tweak any card by hand, and see the exact credit
cost — nothing is charged. Set `dryRun` back to `false` to render.

## Official Zvid nodes

These HTTP Request nodes are deliberately core-only so the workflow imports
untouched anywhere, including n8n Cloud.

On self-hosted n8n you can install **`@zvid/n8n-nodes-zvid`**
(Settings → Community nodes) and swap them for native nodes:

| HTTP Request node | Native replacement |
| --- | --- |
| Validate project (free) | **Zvid** → Render → Validate |
| Submit render | **Zvid** → Render → Create |
| Get render status + Wait | **Zvid Trigger** (render webhook) |

The Zvid Trigger removes the polling loop entirely.

## Publish to Instagram & Facebook

The run ends with `videoUrl` (a ready MP4) and `suggestedCaption`. Wire them
into whichever publishing path you already use:

- **Instagram Reels (Graph API)** — HTTP Request: `POST /{ig-user-id}/media`
  with `media_type=REELS`, `video_url` and `caption`; poll the container
  `status_code` until `FINISHED`; then `POST /{ig-user-id}/media_publish`.
  Needs an Instagram professional account linked to a Facebook Page and the
  `instagram_content_publish` permission.
- **Facebook Page** — HTTP Request: `POST /{page-id}/videos` with
  `file_url` = `videoUrl` and `description` = the caption.
- **Schedulers** — Buffer, Metricool, Later and similar all accept a video
  URL + caption over HTTP.

Post the first few privately (or to a test page) until you like the output.

## ▶ Watch video

Click this node after a run: it downloads the finished MP4 and n8n shows it as
an inline video player in the output panel — no URL to copy, no tab to open.

*Run summary* before it still carries `videoUrl` (plus `jobId` and
`suggestedCaption`) if you want to pipe the result onward to a publish node.

It retries a few times — the CDN can 404 for a moment right after a render
completes — and never fails the run if the download does not work.
